questions.question: The average of 25, 46 and ‘y’ is 11. What is the value of ‘y’?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total sum of 3 numbers = Average × 3 = 11 × 3 = 33

Sum of given numbers = 25 + 46 = 71

Value of y = Total sum − Sum of given numbers

y = 33 − 71 = −38

**∴ The correct answer is −38.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers: 25, 46, and y

Average of these 3 numbers = 11

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69cfcd35a332b12b4b672f193863117dd4323996e082f0ee367db65b93181f44.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Average = (25 + 46 + y) ÷ 3

⇒ 11 = (71 + y) ÷ 3

⇒ 11 × 3 = 71 + y

⇒ 33 = 71 + y

⇒ y = 33 − 71

⇒ y = −38

**∴ The correct answer is −38.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Observations

The sum of n observations is always equal to the product of their average and the total count n. Sum = Average × n.

Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean (average) is always zero. ∑(xᵢ − Average) = 0.

Weighted Average

When different groups have different averages, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: From the top of a tower, the angle of depression of the top of a 10 m high building is 60°. If the distance between the tower and the building is 50√3 m, find the height of the tower.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Angle of depression (θ) = 60° and horizontal distance (d) = 50√3 m.

Height difference between tower and building = d × tan(θ).

Height difference = 50√3 × √3 = 50 × 3 = 150 m.

Total tower height = Building height + Height difference = 10 + 150 = 160 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 160 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of building (h) = 10 m

Distance between tower and building (d) = 50√3 m

Angle of depression = 60°

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/91039c0be91a0eff684d79ee427e05f0b23057165790db6765574b4d91a8d928.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the height of the tower be H.

⇒ Let x be the height of the tower above the building level.

⇒ The angle of depression of the top of the building from the tower top is 60°.

⇒ This is equivalent to the angle of elevation of the tower top from the building top.

⇒ In the right-angled triangle formed above the building level:

⇒ tan 60° = x / 50√3

⇒ √3 = x / 50√3

⇒ x = 50√3 × √3

⇒ x = 50 × 3 = 150 m

⇒ Total height of tower (H) = x + height of building

⇒ H = 150 + 10 = 160 m

**∴ The correct answer is 160 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Depression and Elevation

The angle of depression from point A to point B is numerically equal to the angle of elevation from point B to point A because they are alternate interior angles.

Common Trigonometric Ratios

For height and distance problems: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3.

Standard Height Formula

If two objects are separated by distance d, the height difference is given by h = d × tan(θ), where θ is the angle of elevation/depression between their tops.</p

questions.question: A merchant fixes the sale price of his goods at 42% above the cost price. He sells his goods at a 15% discount marked price. His percentage of profit (rounded off to the nearest integer) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply effective percentage change formula: Profit % = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, Markup (a) = +42 and Discount (b) = −15

Profit % = 42 − 15 + (42 × (−15)) ÷ 100

Profit % = 27 − 6.3 = 20.7%

Rounding off to the nearest integer, we get 21%.

**∴ The correct answer is 21%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given values:

Markup percentage = 42%

Discount percentage = 15%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/88d0999634c6090e5cc9923d4b1005a3633e89fa09e18771053cca56203904ff.png] 

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) be ₹100.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = CP + 42% of CP = 100 + 42 = ₹142.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − 15% of MP.

⇒ SP = 142 − (15 ÷ 100) × 142.

⇒ SP = 142 − 21.3 = ₹120.7.

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 120.7 − 100 = ₹20.7.

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (20.7 ÷ 100) × 100 = 20.7%.

⇒ Rounded to nearest integer = 21%.

**∴ The correct answer is 21%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP) and Discount

Marked price is the price displayed on a product. Discount is always calculated on the MP: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Relationship between CP and MP

The ratio of CP to MP is given by: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

Successive Percentage Formula

If a value is changed by x% and then by y%, the net change is [x + y + (xy ÷ 100)]%. This is useful for markup and discount problems.

questions.question: A set of data presented in the form of a frequency distribution table with class intervals and their respective frequencies had a mode of 48.5. The lower boundary of the modal class was 46.5; the frequency of the modal class was 34; the frequency of the class interval just preceding the modal class was 32 and the frequency of the class interval just succeeding the modal class was 25. What was the width of the modal class?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference between Mode and Lower limit = (f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) × h

48.5 − 46.5 = (34 − 32) ÷ (2 × 34 − 32 − 25) × h

2 = (2 ÷ 11) × h

h = 11

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mode (Mₒ) = 48.5

Lower boundary of modal class (l) = 46.5

Frequency of modal class (f₁) = 34

Frequency of preceding class (f₀) = 32

Frequency of succeeding class (f₂) = 25

**Formula Used:**

Mode = l + [ (f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) ] × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/26f8b4f2a73404a96a90d2bb7de6e66512e8ebd6ffbe43cd3da4be60ed367f21.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 48.5 = 46.5 + [ (34 − 32) ÷ (2 × 34 − 32 − 25) ] × h

⇒ 48.5 − 46.5 = [ 2 ÷ (68 − 57) ] × h

⇒ 2 = (2 ÷ 11) × h

⇒ 2 × 11 = 2h

⇒ 22 = 2h

⇒ h = 22 ÷ 2

⇒ h = 11

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Median for Grouped Data

Median = l + [ (N/2 − cf) ÷ f ] × h, where l is lower limit of median class and cf is cumulative frequency of preceding class.

Empirical Relationship

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean. This formula is used for moderately skewed distributions.

Mean for Grouped Data (Direct Method)

Mean = Σfᵢxᵢ ÷ Σfᵢ, where xᵢ is the class mark (mid-value) of each interval.</p

questions.question: An equilateral triangle ABC surmounts a square BCDE. The value of ∠EAB + 3∠AEB is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Side AB = BC (triangle) and BE = BC (square) ⇒ AB = BE.

∠ABE = ∠ABC + ∠CBE = 60° + 90° = 150°.

In isosceles ΔABE, ∠EAB = ∠AEB = (180° − 150°) ÷ 2 = 15°.

Value of ∠EAB + 3∠AEB = 15° + 3(15°) = 15° + 45° = 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ABC is an equilateral triangle and BCDE is a square.

**Formula:** Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°; Angles in square = 90°; Angles in equilateral triangle = 60°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/79bf07f9bd2e8ad12bfdc1ee08b6158cf7b1999bb262f816499c454f8f587dee.png] 

⇒ In equilateral ΔABC, AB = BC = AC and ∠ABC = 60°.

⇒ In square BCDE, BC = CD = DE = BE and ∠EBC = 90°.

⇒ Total ∠ABE = ∠ABC + ∠EBC = 60° + 90° = 150°.

⇒ Since AB = BC and BE = BC, we have AB = BE.

⇒ In ΔABE, ∠EAB = ∠AEB (angles opposite to equal sides).

⇒ ∠ABE + ∠EAB + ∠AEB = 180°

⇒ 150° + 2 × ∠AEB = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠AEB = 30° ⇒ ∠AEB = 15°

⇒ Similarly, ∠EAB = 15°.

⇒ Required value = ∠EAB + 3∠AEB = 15° + 3(15°) = 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equilateral Triangle Properties

All three sides are equal in length, and each internal angle measures exactly 60°.

Square Properties

A square is a regular quadrilateral with four equal sides and four equal angles of 90°.

Isosceles Triangle Theorem

If two sides of a triangle are equal, then the angles opposite those sides are also equal.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.</p

questions.question: The marks obtained by 15 students out of a maximum of 25 in a test are given as 13, 11, 16, 15, 18, 12, 13, 14, 10, 22, 15, 21, 20, 17 and 24. Find the product of the modes of this set of data.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify frequencies: 13 appears 2 times, 15 appears 2 times.

All other numbers (10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22, 24) appear only once.

The highest frequency is 2, so the modes are 13 and 15.

Product of modes = 13 × 15 = 195.

**∴ The correct answer is 195.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Data set = {13, 11, 16, 15, 18, 12, 13, 14, 10, 22, 15, 21, 20, 17, 24}

**Formula:** Mode is the observation(s) with the highest frequency in the data set.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/39e84d02666bc851724a2411fd5a5ba9495ac327f9f5535dc5066813e693d4a0.png] 

⇒ Arranging the data in ascending order: 10, 11, 12, 13, 13, 14, 15, 15, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22, 24.

⇒ Frequency count:

⇒ 10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22, 24 → 1 time each.

⇒ 13 → 2 times.

⇒ 15 → 2 times.

⇒ Since 13 and 15 have the highest frequency (2), there are two modes.

⇒ Modes = 13 and 15.

⇒ Product of modes = 13 × 15 = 195.

**∴ The correct answer is 195.**

**__Additional Information__**

Mode of a Dataset

The mode is the value that occurs most frequently in a data set. A set can have one mode (unimodal), two modes (bimodal), or more (multimodal).

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Mean and Median

Mean is the average (sum ÷ count). Median is the middle value when data is arranged in ascending or descending order.</p

questions.question: Two friends A and B started a business by investing Rs. 1,50,000 and Rs. 2,50,000, respectively. They agreed to distribute their earnings in the same ratio of their investments. After an year, the profit earned was Rs. 6,00,000. Each of them added Rs. 50,000 to their respective profits and invested in a different project. If this project gave an yield of Rs. 4,20,000, then A’s share in the profit is:
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Ratio of investments A : B = 1,50,000 : 2,50,000 = 3 : 5. Divide profit ₹6,00,000 in 3 : 5 → A = ₹2,25,000 and B = ₹3,75,000. New investment ratio = (2,25,000 + 50,000) : (3,75,000 + 50,000) = 2,75,000 : 4,25,000 = 11 : 17. A’s share in new profit = (11 ÷ 28) × 4,20,000 = 11 × 15,000 = ₹1,65,000. **∴ The correct answer is ₹1,65,000.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** **Given:** Initial investment A = ₹1,50,000 | Initial investment B = ₹2,50,000 Profit Project 1 = ₹6,00,000 | Profit Project 2 = ₹4,20,000 **Formula Used:** Profit Ratio = (Capital₁ × Time₁) : (Capital₂ × Time₂) [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/33d9d1be121d28e3ee0db87700d57f33005086df051a140be693991a05aab716.png] ⇒ Investment Ratio A : B = 1,50,000 : 2,50,000 = 3 : 5 ⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 3 + 5 = 8 units ⇒ 8 units = ₹6,00,000 ⇒ 1 unit = 6,00,000 ÷ 8 = ₹75,000 ⇒ A’s profit share (Project 1) = 3 × 75,000 = ₹2,25,000 ⇒ B’s profit share (Project 1) = 5 × 75,000 = ₹3,75,000 ⇒ A’s investment (Project 2) = 2,25,000 + 50,000 = ₹2,75,000 ⇒ B’s investment (Project 2) = 3,75,000 + 50,000 = ₹4,25,000 ⇒ New Ratio A : B = 2,75,000 : 4,25,000 = 11 : 17 ⇒ Total ratio units (Project 2) = 11 + 17 = 28 units ⇒ A’s share in Project 2 profit = (11 ÷ 28) × 4,20,000 ⇒ A’s share = 11 × 15,000 = ₹1,65,000 **∴ The correct answer is ₹1,65,000.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** Partnership Profit Sharing Rule Profit is always distributed in the ratio of the product of Investment (Capital) and Time: Profit Ratio = (C₁ × T₁) : (C₂ × T₂). questions.question: The ratio of the length, width and height of a closed cuboid is given as 6 ∶ 3 ∶ 2. The total surface area of this cuboid is given as 1800 cm². Find the volume (in cm³) of this cuboid.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of dimensions L : W : H = 6 : 3 : 2.

TSA ratio units = 2 × (6×3 + 3×2 + 2×6) = 2 × (18 + 6 + 12) = 72 units².

72 units² = 1800 cm² ⇒ 1 unit² = 25 ⇒ 1 unit = 5 cm.

Volume = (6 × 3 × 2) × (5)³ = 36 × 125 = 4500 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 4500 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of length (l), width (w), and height (h) = 6 : 3 : 2

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 1800 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area of Cuboid = 2(lw + wh + hl)

Volume of Cuboid = l × w × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7d857f632f4662067d3a3850e106dbb603d5f4d516e62fa2f3a052ee960669c0.png] 

Let the length, width, and height be 6x, 3x, and 2x respectively.

⇒ TSA = 2[(6x × 3x) + (3x × 2x) + (2x × 6x)]

⇒ 1800 = 2[18x² + 6x² + 12x²]

⇒ 900 = 36x²

⇒ x² = 900 ÷ 36

⇒ x² = 25

⇒ x = √25 = 5

Now, dimensions of the cuboid are:

⇒ Length (l) = 6 × 5 = 30 cm

⇒ Width (w) = 3 × 5 = 15 cm

⇒ Height (h) = 2 × 5 = 10 cm

Volume of the cuboid:

⇒ V = l × w × h

⇒ V = 30 × 15 × 10

⇒ V = 4500 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 4500 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Lateral Surface Area of Cuboid

It is the area of the four side walls of the cuboid, calculated as LSA = 2h(l + w).

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The length of the longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid is given by d = √(l² + w² + h²).

Cube Properties

For a cube of side 'a', Volume = a³ and Total Surface Area = 6a².</p

questions.question: B purchased 15 kg apples at the rate of Rs. 180 per kg from a wholesaler who uses a weight of 950 grams for the kg weight. B sold all these apples at Rs. 180 per kg but used a weight of 750 grams for the kg weight. Find the percentage profit earned by B in the transaction (correct to 2 places of decimal).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In dishonest dealer problems where buying and selling rates are same:

Profit % = [(Wholesaler Weight − B's Weight) ÷ B's Weight] × 100

Profit % = [(950 − 750) ÷ 750] × 100

Profit % = [200 ÷ 750] × 100 = (4 ÷ 15) × 100 = 26.666...

**∴ The correct answer is 26.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate of purchase = ₹180/kg | Weight received from wholesaler = 950 g for every 1000 g

Rate of sale = ₹180/kg | Weight given to customer = 750 g for every 1000 g

Total apples purchased = 15 kg

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f7ec5034186304ceb191e61882e5d4a41097d0ce73873fdaa65e55c22e74f480.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Actual quantity received by B = 15 kg × (950/1000) = 14.25 kg

⇒ Total Cost Price (CP) for B = 15 × ₹180 = ₹2700 (since B pays for 15kg)

⇒ B sells 750 g as 1 kg. So, 14.25 kg is sold as = 14.25 ÷ 0.750 = 19 units of 1 kg

⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) for B = 19 × ₹180 = ₹3420

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 3420 − 2700 = ₹720

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (720 ÷ 2700) × 100 = 72000 ÷ 2700 = 720 ÷ 27 = 80 ÷ 3

⇒ Profit % = 26.666...

**∴ The correct answer is 26.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer cheats while buying and selling, the overall profit multiplier is (Buying Factor × Selling Factor). Profit % = [(&text{True Weight} + &text{Gain while buying}) ÷ (&text{True Weight} − &text{Loss while selling}) − 1] × 100.

Ratio Method for Profit

For dishonest weights, CP : SP = Weight Given : Weight Charged. If the price per kg also changes, multiply the ratios accordingly.

Effective Profit %

If a person uses x% less weight, the profit % is [x ÷ (100 − x)] × 100. In this case, B uses 25% less weight (250g/1000g) on his end, but he also received 5% less weight from the wholesaler.

questions.question: If P(A cup B)=(5)/(9), P(bar{A} cup bar{B})=(13)/(27), P(A)=(11)/(18), then the odds against the event B are:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Find P(A ∩ B) using De Morgan Law: P(A ∩ B) = 1 − P(Ā ∪ B̄) = 1 − 13/27 = 14/27.

Calculate P(B) using Addition Rule: P(B) = P(A ∪ B) + P(A ∩ B) − P(A) = 5/9 + 14/27 − 11/18.

Using LCM 54: P(B) = (30 + 28 − 33) / 54 = 25/54.

Odds against B = P(B̄) : P(B) = (54 − 25) : 25 = 29 : 25.

**∴ The correct answer is 29/25.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

P(A ∪ B) = 5/9

P(Ā ∪ B̄) = 13/27

P(A) = 11/18

**Formula Used:**

1. De Morgan's Law: P(Ā ∪ B̄) = P((A ∩ B)̄) = 1 − P(A ∩ B)

2. Addition Theorem: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)

3. Odds against event B = P(B̄) / P(B) = (1 − P(B)) / P(B)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d96a29162179eb17ebfa1bb8cefe906f52464e56aa526f418ae8d9ce63ab1154.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ P(A ∩ B) = 1 − P(Ā ∪ B̄)

⇒ P(A ∩ B) = 1 − 13/27 = 14/27

⇒ P(B) = P(A ∪ B) − P(A) + P(A ∩ B)

⇒ P(B) = 5/9 − 11/18 + 14/27

⇒ LCM of 9, 18, 27 is 54.

⇒ P(B) = (30 − 33 + 28) / 54 = 25/54

⇒ P(B̄) = 1 − 25/54 = 29/54

⇒ Odds against B = P(B̄) / P(B) = (29/54) / (25/54)

⇒ Odds against B = 29/25

**∴ The correct answer is 29/25.**

**__Additional Information__**

De Morgan's Laws

For any two events A and B, P(Ā ∩ B̄) = P((A ∪ B)̄) and P(Ā ∪ B̄) = P((A ∩ B)̄).

Odds in Favor vs Odds Against

Odds in favor of an event E are P(E) : P(Ē). Odds against an event E are P(Ē) : P(E).

Probability Addition Theorem

For any events A and B, P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B). If they are mutually exclusive, P(A ∩ B) = 0.</p

questions.question: The average weight of the first thirteen persons among fourteen persons is 78 kg. The weight of the 14th person is 39 kg more than the average weight of all the fourteen persons. Find the weight of the 14th person.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The extra weight of the 14th person (39 kg) is distributed among the first 13 persons to equalize their average to the overall average.

Total Average = Average of 13 persons + (Extra weight ÷ 13)

Total Average = 78 + (39 ÷ 13) = 78 + 3 = 81 kg

Weight of 14th person = Total Average + Extra = 81 + 39 = 120 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 120 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of 13 persons = 78 kg

Weight of 14th person = Average of 14 persons + 39 kg

**Formula Used:**

questions.question: Three cards are drawn one after another with replacement from a pack of cards. What is the probability of getting first card a Jack, second card a black card, and third card an even numbered card?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Probability of independent events with replacement = P(A) × P(B) × P(C)

P(Jack) = 4/52 = 1/13

P(Black Card) = 26/52 = 1/2

P(Even Numbered Card) = 20/52 = 5/13 (Even cards are 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 per suit)

Total Probability = (1/13) × (1/2) × (5/13) = 5/338

**∴ The correct answer is 5/338.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total cards in a pack = 52

Condition: With replacement (Events are independent)

**Formula Used:**

Probability P(E) = Number of favorable outcomes ÷ Total number of outcomes

For independent events, P(A and B and C) = P(A) × P(B) × P(C)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a0774277e1c102c694347d2a995bbf73681265f1dfc592bd8b1b4236055fae0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total cards in a pack = 52

⇒ Number of Jacks = 4 (Jack of Spades, Clubs, Hearts, Diamonds)

⇒ P(First card is a Jack) = 4/52 = 1/13

⇒ Number of black cards = 26 (13 Spades + 13 Clubs)

⇒ P(Second card is black) = 26/52 = 1/2

⇒ Numbered cards are 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. Even numbered cards = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}

⇒ Total even numbered cards = 5 per suit × 4 suits = 20

⇒ P(Third card is an even numbered card) = 20/52 = 5/13

⇒ Combined Probability = (1/13) × (1/2) × (5/13)

⇒ Combined Probability = 5 / (13 × 2 × 13) = 5 / (26 × 13)

⇒ Combined Probability = 5/338

**∴ The correct answer is 5/338.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Independent Events with Replacement

When objects are replaced, the total number of outcomes remains the same for every draw, making the events independent.

Dependent Events without Replacement

If cards were drawn without replacement, the denominator would decrease: P(A) × P(B|A) × P(C|A,B) with totals 52, 51, and 50 respectively.

Face Cards and Numbered Cards

A standard deck has 12 face cards (J, Q, K) and 36 numbered cards (2 to 10). Ace is usually not counted as a numbered card in competitive exams unless specified.</p

questions.question: At a certain time in a park, the number of heads and the number of legs of monkeys and human visitors were counted, and it was found that there were 54 heads and 148 legs. Find the number of monkeys in the park.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the number of 4-legged animals (Monkeys) in a group of 2-legged and 4-legged animals:

Number of Monkeys = (Total Legs − 2 × Total Heads) ÷ 2

⇒ Number of Monkeys = (148 − 2 × 54) ÷ 2

⇒ Number of Monkeys = (148 − 108) ÷ 2 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20 monkeys.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of heads = 54

Total number of legs = 148

Number of legs for a human = 2

Number of legs for a monkey = 4

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5c41b5239d63110ce5345b33168f4104e57ae2900253c554050fe2d84e515430.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the number of monkeys be M and humans be H.

⇒ Total heads: M + H = 54 → (Eq. 1)

⇒ Total legs: 4M + 2H = 148 → (Eq. 2)

⇒ Multiply (Eq. 1) by 2: 2M + 2H = 108 → (Eq. 3)

⇒ Subtract (Eq. 3) from (Eq. 2): (4M − 2M) + (2H − 2H) = 148 − 108

⇒ 2M = 40

⇒ M = 40 ÷ 2 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20 monkeys.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alligation Method for Heads/Legs

Ratio of 4-legged to 2-legged animals = (Average legs per head − 2) : (4 − Average legs per head).

Linear Equation Method

Solving systems of equations x + y = Total Heads and Ax + By = Total Legs, where A and B are the number of legs per animal.

Assumption Shortcut

Assume all animals have 2 legs: Total legs would be 2 × Heads. Any excess legs (Total Legs − Calculated Legs) belong to the 4-legged animals in pairs.</p

questions.question: Vipin travels one-third of the distance of a journey at a speed of 30 km/h and the remaining distance at a speed of 40 km/h. If he took a total of 12 hours to complete the journey, what was the total distance (in km) of the journey?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

LCM of speeds 30 and 40 = 120.

Let 1/3 distance = 120 km, then 2/3 distance = 240 km.

Total hypothetical distance = 120 + 240 = 360 km.

Total time taken = (120 ÷ 30) + (240 ÷ 40) = 4 + 6 = 10 hours.

Given time is 12 hours ⇒ Actual distance = (360 ÷ 10) × 12 = 432 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 432 km.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Time = 12 hours

Speed 1 (for 1/3 distance) = 30 km/h

Speed 2 (for 2/3 distance) = 40 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7cd27194270ca11657c758ebd1af0dcbc5ea3ee472e3cdd3788e773b740b48cd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total distance be x km.

⇒ Distance 1 = x/3 km and Distance 2 = 2x/3 km.

⇒ Time 1 + Time 2 = 12

⇒ (x/3) ÷ 30 + (2x/3) ÷ 40 = 12

⇒ x/90 + 2x/120 = 12

⇒ x/90 + x/60 = 12

⇒ (2x + 3x) ÷ 180 = 12

⇒ 5x ÷ 180 = 12

⇒ x ÷ 36 = 12

⇒ x = 36 × 12 = 432 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 432 km.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed Formula

Average speed is calculated as Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If the distances are equal, the formula is 2uv ÷ (u+v).

Distance, Speed, and Time Relation

Distance = Speed × Time. When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S₁ ÷ S₂ = T₂ ÷ T₁).

Conversion of Units

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p

Given tan y = 3/5 → cot y = 5/3

h = 150 ÷ (5/2 + 5/3) = 150 ÷ (25/6) = 150 × 6 ÷ 25

questions.question: The cost of 2 pencils and 3 pens is Rs. 55 and the cost of 7 pencils and 2 pens is Rs. 65. What is the total price (in Rs.) of one pen and one pencil?

Let cost of Pencil = x and Pen = y.

Equations: 2x + 3y = 55 and 7x + 2y = 65.

Subtracting both: (7x − 2x) − (3y − 2y) = 65 − 55 ⇒ 5x − y = 10 ⇒ y = 5x − 10.

Substitute y in first: 2x + 3(5x − 10) = 55 ⇒ 17x = 85 ⇒ x = 5 and y = 15.

Total cost (x + y) = 5 + 15 = 20.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹20.**

⇒ 21x + 6y = 195 ... (4)

⇒ Subtract (3) from (4): (21x − 4x) = (195 − 110) ⇒ 17x = 85

⇒ Put x = 5 in (1): 2(5) + 3y = 55 ⇒ 10 + 3y = 55 ⇒ 3y = 45 ⇒ y = 15

⇒ Total price of one pen and one pencil = x + y = 5 + 15 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is ₹20.**

questions.question: A six-digit number 11p9q4 is divisible by 24. Then the greatest possible value for pq is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For divisibility by 24, the number must be divisible by both 8 and 3.

Last three digits 9q4 ÷ 8 ⇒ 904, 944, 984 are divisible by 8, so q ∈ {0, 4, 8}.

Sum of digits (1+1+p+9+q+4) = 15+p+q must be divisible by 3 ⇒ (p+q) must be a multiple of 3.

Case 1: If q = 8, max p = 7 (as 7+8=15) ⇒ pq = 7 × 8 = 56.

Case 2: If q = 4, max p = 8 (as 8+4=12) ⇒ pq = 8 × 4 = 32.

Case 3: If q = 0, max p = 9 (as 9+0=9) ⇒ pq = 9 × 0 = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number = 11p9q4, Divisor = 24.

**Property:** A number is divisible by 24 if it is divisible by 8 (last 3 digits) and 3 (sum of digits).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1dad386f43ff244d5f26709a26eba64e18a6223af34d006312b69d65e951201b.png] 

⇒ Divisibility by 8: The last three digits 9q4 must be divisible by 8.

⇒ 900 + 10q + 4 = 904 + 10q. Since 904 is divisible by 8 (904 = 8 × 113), 10q must be divisible by 8.

⇒ Possible values for q are 0, 4, and 8.

⇒ Divisibility by 3: Sum of digits = 1 + 1 + p + 9 + q + 4 = 15 + p + q.

⇒ For (15 + p + q) to be divisible by 3, (p + q) must be 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, or 18.

⇒ If q = 8: p + 8 = 9, 12, 15 ⇒ p = 1, 4, 7. Max pq = 7 × 8 = 56.

⇒ If q = 4: p + 4 = 6, 9, 12 ⇒ p = 2, 5, 8. Max pq = 8 × 4 = 32.

⇒ If q = 0: p + 0 = 0, 3, 6, 9 ⇒ p = 0, 3, 6, 9. Max pq = 9 × 0 = 0.

⇒ Comparing all products, the greatest value is 56.

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

Divisibility by 8

A number is divisible by 8 if its last three digits are divisible by 8 or are zeros.

Divisibility by 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of all its individual digits is divisible by 3.

Composite Divisibility Rule

If a number is divisible by two co-prime numbers a and b, then it is also divisible by their product (a × b).</p

questions.question: The compound interest on Rs. 10,000 at 20% per annum is Rs. 4,641. If the compounding is done half-yearly, then for how many years was the sum invested?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate for half-yearly compounding = 20% ÷ 2 = 10%.

Ratio of Amount to Principal (A/P) = 14,641 / 10,000 = (1.4641/1).

Since (1 + 10/100)ⁿ = 1.1ⁿ, we observe that 1.1⁴ = 1.4641.

Total periods (n) = 4 half-years.

Time in years = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Principal (P) = Rs. 10,000

Compound Interest (CI) = Rs. 4,641

Rate (R) = 20% per annum (Compounded half-yearly)

Formula Used: Amount (A) = P × (1 + r/100)ⁿ, where r is the rate per period and n is the number of periods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/11fd7d20ebeb150c184c8dd5932c3400613a6ec44c3e59fbfa71d9b04e842ff8.png] 

Calculations:

⇒ Amount (A) = Principal + Compound Interest

⇒ A = 10,000 + 4,641 = 14,641

⇒ For half-yearly compounding, Rate (r) = 20% ÷ 2 = 10% per half-year.

⇒ Let the total periods be n.

⇒ 14,641 = 10,000 × (1 + 10/100)ⁿ

⇒ 14,641 / 10,000 = (11/10)ⁿ

⇒ 1.4641 = (1.1)ⁿ

⇒ (1.1)⁴ = (1.1)ⁿ

⇒ n = 4 periods

⇒ Since each period is 6 months, Total Time = 4 × 6 = 24 months = 2 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CI Compounded Half-Yearly

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the annual rate is divided by 2 and the time (in years) is multiplied by 2.

CI Compounded Quarterly

When interest is compounded quarterly, the annual rate is divided by 4 and the time (in years) is multiplied by 4.

Effective Rate Formula

For two periods with rate r%, the effective rate is [r + r + (r × r)/100] %.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, CI − SI = P × (R/100)². For 3 years, CI − SI = P × (R/100)² × (3 + R/100).</p

questions.question: Hari, Kamal and Lalit contested an election in which 6050 votes were polled and none of the votes were invalid. Kamal got 42% more votes than the total votes obtained by Hari and Lalit together. If Lalit obtained only 8% of the total polled votes, find the number of votes obtained by Hari.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Kamal : (Hari + Lalit) = 142 : 100 = 71 : 50.

Total parts = 71 + 50 = 121 units.

121 units = 6050 ⇒ 1 unit = 50.

Hari + Lalit = 50 × 50 = 2500.

Lalit = 8% of 6050 = 484.

Hari = 2500 − 484 = 2016.

**∴ The correct answer is 2016 votes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total polled votes = 6050

Lalit's share = 8% of total votes

Kamal's share = (Hari + Lalit) + 42% of (Hari + Lalit)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/01feec75455bd74a61d840b52546a08251bc28931bd0f0c4746238f5798d6b4f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Votes obtained by Lalit = 8% of 6050

⇒ Lalit = (8 × 6050) ÷ 100 = 484

⇒ Let votes obtained by (Hari + Lalit) = x

⇒ Kamal's votes = x + 0.42x = 1.42x

⇒ Total votes = Kamal + (Hari + Lalit)

⇒ 6050 = 1.42x + x

⇒ 6050 = 2.42x

⇒ x = 6050 ÷ 2.42 = 2500

⇒ Hari + Lalit = 2500

⇒ Hari + 484 = 2500

⇒ Hari = 2500 − 484 = 2016

**∴ The correct answer is 2016 votes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Election Vote Concepts

Total Votes Polled = Valid Votes + Invalid Votes. In this case, all polled votes are valid.

Percentage Comparison

If A is r% more than B, then A = B × (1 + r/100). If A is r% less than B, then A = B × (1 − r/100).

Ratio Partitioning

To divide a total 'T' into a ratio a : b, the first part is [a / (a+b)] × T and the second part is [b / (a+b)] × T.</p

questions.question: A and B can complete a job together in 12.5 days; B and C can complete the same job together in 18.75 days, while C and A can complete the same job together in 15 days. In how many days will A, B and C together be able to complete the same job alongside D, who is only 40% as efficient as C?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(12.5, 18.75, 15) = 75 units.

Eff(A+B) = 6, Eff(B+C) = 4, Eff(C+A) = 5.

Combined Eff(A+B+C) = (6 + 4 + 5) ÷ 2 = 7.5 units/day.

Eff(C) = 7.5 − 6 = 1.5 units/day | Eff(D) = 40% of 1.5 = 0.6 units/day.

Total Time = 75 ÷ (7.5 + 0.6) = 75 ÷ 8.1 = 250/27 = 9 7/27 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 7/27 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time (A + B) = 12.5 days = 25/2 days

Time (B + C) = 18.75 days = 75/4 days

Time (C + A) = 15 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × Efficiency (A + B + C) = 15

⇒ Efficiency (A + B + C) = 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of C = Efficiency (A + B + C) − Efficiency (A + B)

Work and Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. If a person takes 'n' days to complete a work, their efficiency is 1/n per day.

Combined Work Formula

For pairs (A+B, B+C, C+A), individual efficiency of A = [Eff(A+B) + Eff(C+A) − Eff(B+C)] ÷ 2.

Efficiency Ratios

questions.question: The average age of A, B and C is 20 years. Two years ago the sum of the ages of A and B was 6 more than that of C. Find the present age of C.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total present age of A, B and C = 20 × 3 = 60 years.

Two years ago, (A − 2) + (B − 2) = (C − 2) + 6 ⇒ (A + B) − C = 8.

We have: (A + B) + C = 60 and (A + B) − C = 8.

By subtracting the equations: 2C = 60 − 8 = 52 ⇒ C = 26 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 26 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average age of A, B, C = 20 years.

Condition 2 years ago: (Sum of A & B) = (Age of C) + 6.

**Formula Used:**

Total Age = Average × Number of persons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e977c6c47a2aa9d4d8f82d8894221415cdc885a18d51846c5e827bec13b7660c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Present sum A + B + C = 20 × 3 = 60 --- (i)

⇒ Ages 2 years ago: (A−2), (B−2), (C−2)

⇒ According to question: (A − 2) + (B − 2) = (C − 2) + 6

⇒ A + B − 4 = C + 4

⇒ A + B − C = 8 --- (ii)

⇒ From (i), A + B = 60 − C

⇒ Substitute in (ii): (60 − C) − C = 8

⇒ 60 − 2C = 8

⇒ 2C = 52

⇒ C = 26 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 26 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Age Concept

If the average age of n persons is X years, then after t years, the average age will be (X + t) years.

Sum of Ages

To find the sum of ages of a group, multiply the average age by the number of members in that group (Sum = Average × n).

Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two individuals remains constant regardless of the number of years passed.</p

questions.question: One chord of a circle is given as 20.5 cm. Then the radius (r) of the circle must be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a circle, the diameter is the longest possible chord.

Any other chord must be less than or equal to the diameter.

Mathematically, Diameter (2r) ≥ Chord length.

2r ≥ 20.5 ⇒ r ≥ 10.25.

**∴ The correct answer is r ≥ 10.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of chord = 20.5 cm

Radius of the circle = r

**Formula/Property Used:**

Diameter of a circle (D) = 2 × radius (r)

Geometric Property: Diameter ≥ Any Chord of the circle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b448ddde3150058335d0b9a0b734c6f01c8a87ff9481a60a567a23796a96aad5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Diameter ≥ Chord

⇒ 2r ≥ 20.5 cm

⇒ r ≥ 20.5 ÷ 2

⇒ r ≥ 10.25

**∴ The correct answer is r ≥ 10.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Longest Chord Property

The diameter is the unique chord that passes through the center of the circle and is the maximum length of any chord.

Chord Perpendicularity

A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord into two equal halves.

Chord Distance from Center

Longer chords are always closer to the center of the circle compared to shorter chords. The diameter (the longest chord) has a distance of zero from the center.</p
